Recipes.name: Dum Biriyani
Recipes.ingredients:
Main Ingredients (for ~1 kg meat/rice)
• Rice: 1 kg long-grain aged Basmati rice (soaked for 30 minutes)
• Protein: 1 kg chicken (bone-in, cut into pieces) or mutton
• Dairy & Fat:
	• 250 ml (about 1 cup) plain yogurt or thick curd
	• 250 ml cooking oil
	• 2 to 3 tablespoons ghee (clarified butter)
	• ½ cup milk (for soaking saffron)
• Aromatics & Herbs:
	• 2 to 3 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
	• 4 to 6 green chilies (slid or made into a paste)
	• 1 cup fresh mint leaves (finely chopped)
	• 1 cup fresh coriander/cilantro leaves (finely chopped)
	• 2 teaspoons lemon juice
Recipes.instructions:
Marinade & Chicken Prep
• Marinate the chicken: Mix 1 kg bone-in chicken with 125g to 1/2 cup thick yogurt (curd), ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, salt, lemon juice, half of your fried onions (beresta), and biryani masala. Let it rest for at least 1 to 3 hours (or overnight in the fridge).
• Cook the base (For Pakki/Semi-Cooked style): In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat oil or ghee, add whole spices (bay leaf, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, shahi jeera), and cook the marinated chicken partially or until a thick gravy forms and oil separates. (Note: In Kacchi style, raw marinated chicken is used directly at the bottom of the pot).

 Rice Boiling
• Soak the rice: Wash and soak 3 to 4 cups of aged Basmati rice for 30 minutes.
• Par-boil the rice: Boil water in a large pot with whole spices (bay leaf, cloves, cardamom, shahi jeera) and plenty of salt until it tastes like seawater. Add the drained rice and cook until it is about 70% to 80% done (firm with a slight bite). Drain immediately.

Layering (The Assembly)
• First layer: In a wide, heavy-bottomed pot (or Dutch oven), place your cooked chicken gravy or raw marinated chicken at the base.
• Herb & onion sprinkle: Add a handful of freshly chopped mint leaves, cilantro (coriander leaves), and crispy fried onions.
• Rice layer: Gently spread the hot, 70% par-boiled basmati rice evenly over the chicken.
• Top dressings: Drizzle warm saffron-soaked milk, melted ghee (clarified butter), a splash of rose water or kewra water, remaining fried onions, mint, and cilantro over the top rice layer.

The Dum (Slow Steam Cooking)
• Seal the pot: Cover the pot tightly with a well-fitted lid. Seal the edges using a rolled-out chapati dough or heavy aluminum foil so no steam can escape.
• Heat placement: Place a heavy iron tawa (griddle) on the stove, set the sealed biryani pot on top of it.
• Slow cook: Cook on high heat for the first 5 to 10 minutes to build steam, then lower the flame to the minimum setting and cook for 20 to 30 minutes.
• Rest: Turn off the heat and let it rest undisturbed for 10 to 15 minutes before breaking the seal. Open gently from the side so each plate gets a mix of white rice, saffron rice, and tender meat
Recipes.description: Dum biryani is a traditional South Asian rice dish where marinated meat (or vegetables) and partially cooked rice are layered together in a heavy pot, sealed airtight (often with dough), and slow-cooked over a low fire

Recipes.name: Masala-Dosa
Recipes.ingredients:
Dosa Batter Ingredients
• Idli rice or parboiled rice (1.5 cups)
• Urad dal (husked black gram, 1/2 to 1 cup)
• Chana dal (split Bengal gram, 1 tablespoon)
• Flattened rice (poha, 1/4 cup)
• Fenugreek seeds (methi seeds, 1/2 teaspoon or ~20 seeds)
• Rock salt or sea salt (1/2 teaspoon)
• Water (for soaking and grinding)

Potato Masala (Filling) Ingredients
• Boiled and mashed potatoes (3 to 4 medium-sized)
• Oil or ghee (1 to 2 tablespoons)
• Mustard seeds (1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon)
• Cumin seeds (1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon)
• Chana dal / Urad dal (1/4 to 1 tablespoon for tempering)
• Asafoetida (hing, a pinch)
• Curry leaves (8 to 10 leaves)
• Onions (1 to 2 medium, thinly sliced or chopped)
• Green chilies (1 to 2, finely chopped)
• Ginger (1 teaspoon, finely chopped or grated)
• Turmeric powder (1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon)
• Fresh coriander leaves (chopped, for garnish)
• Salt (to taste)
• Butter or oil (for roasting the dosa on the pan)
Recipes.instructions:
1. Ingredients
• Batter: 2 cups idli rice, 0.5 cup urad dal (split black gram), 0.5 teaspoon fenugreek (methi) seeds, 0.25 cup poha (flattened rice), and salt to taste.
• Potato Masala: 3 boiled and peeled potatoes, 1 sliced onion, 1 green chili (finely chopped), 0.5 teaspoon mustard seeds, 1 teaspoon urad dal, 1 teaspoon chana dal, a pinch of asafoetida , curry leaves, 0.25 teaspoon turmeric powder, 1 tablespoon oil, and fresh coriander leaves.

2. Making the Batter
• Soak: Wash the idli rice, urad dal, and fenugreek seeds together or separately, and soak them in water for 4 to 5 hours. Soak the poha for 30 minutes before grinding.
• Grind: Blend the soaked dal, fenugreek seeds, and poha into a smooth, fluffy batter, and blend the rice to a slightly fine or semi-smooth consistency.
• Ferment: Combine the batters in a large bowl with salt, mix well, and let it ferment in a warm place for 8 to 16 hours until bubbly and doubled in size


3. Preparing the Potato Masala
• Temper: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a pan over medium heat. Add mustard seeds and let them crackle.
• Sauté: Add urad dal, chana dal, asafoetida, and curry leaves, sautéing until the dals turn light golden. Add chopped ginger, green chilies, and sliced onions, cooking until the onions are translucent.
• Season: Stir in the turmeric powder, salt, and a splash of water (about 0.3 cup).
• Mash: Add the boiled, peeled, and crumbled potatoes, mixing well and lightly mashing with the back of a spoon. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, then garnish with fresh coriander leaves.

4. Cooking the Dosa
• Heat Tawa: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa (griddle) over medium heat, then wipe it lightly with a few drops of oil using a cloth or tissue.
• Spread Batter: Pour a ladleful of fermented batter into the center of the tawa and use the back of the ladle or a small bowl to spread it outward in a thin, circular motion.
• Drizzle Oil: Drizzle a little oil or ghee around the edges and across the top.
• Add Masala & Fold: When the bottom turns golden brown and crisp, place 2 to 3 tablespoons of the potato masala in the center, fold the dosa over the filling, and remove from heat
Recipes.description: A Masala Dosa is a classic South Indian dish made of a thin, crispy, golden-brown crepe wrapped around a spiced potato filling

Recipes.name: Dynamic-Burger
Recipes.ingredients:
Dynamite Beef Burger (Home Chef Recipe Style)
• Protein: Ground Beef
• Potatoes / Side or Crunch: Russet Potatoes (often made into wedges or fries)
• Produce & Fresh Elements: Avocado, Shallot, and Jalapeno Pepper
• Bread: Sesame Rolls
• Cheese: Pepperjack Cheese Slices
• Sauce & Seasoning: Garlic Aioli, Fiesta Seasoning, AP Flour, and Garlic Salt

Southern-Style Dynamite Burger
• Patty: Ground chuck seasoned with Montreal Steak Seasoning and Worcestershire Sauce
• Toppings: Bacon, Jalapeno Pimento Cheese, and Bread and Butter Pickles
• Sauce: Chipotle Comeback Sauce (made with Duke's Mayo, chipotle Tabasco, ketchup, onion flakes, and pickle relish)
• Bread: Potato Buns slathered with mayonnaise

Dynamite Sauce (for Chicken or Beef Burgers)
• Base: Mayonnaise and a splash of Heavy Cream
• Heat & Flavor: Sriracha Sauce, Hot Chili Sauce, Soya Sauce, and a touch of Honey
• Aromatics: Garlic Powder, White Pepper, and Salt
Recipes.instructions:
1. Preheat the Pan or Grill: Heat a cast-iron skillet, heavy pan, or grill over medium-high heat until hot.
2. Season the Patties: Season the beef patties generously with salt and pepper right before placing them in the heat.
3. Sear the Meat: Cook the patties for 3 to 4 minutes per side without pressing down on them, letting a deep brown crust form.
4. Melt the Cheese: Add a slice of cheese to the patty during the last 1 to 2 minutes of cooking and cover briefly to melt.
5. Toast the Buns: Lightly toast the buttered buns on the skillet or grill for 15 to 20 seconds.
6. Rest the Patty: Let the cooked beef rest for about 3 to 5 minutes so the natural juices stay locked inside.
7. Assemble: Spread the dynamite sauce on both the top and bottom buns, layer the lettuce, pickles, onions, and tomato, add the hot cheeseburger patty, and close the sandwich.
Recipes.description: A Dynamic Beef Burger typically features a savory beef patty paired with cheese, carrot, cos lettuce, mayonnaise, and tomato sauce

Recipes.name: Puttu & Kadala Curry
Recipes.ingredients:
• Rice Flour: 2 cups puttu podi (roasted coarse rice flour)
• Coconut: 1 cup fresh grated coconut (for layering)
• Water: About 3/4 cup water (added gradually)
• Salt: 3/4 tsp salt

Kadala Curry Ingredients

• Black Chickpeas: 1 cup black chana (kala chana / karuppu kadalai), soaked overnight
• Aromatics & Base:
	• 1 to 2 onions or small shallots (finely sliced)
	• 1 to 2 tomatoes (chopped)
	• 1 inch ginger
	• 4 to 5 garlic cloves
	• 1 to 3 green chillies (slit)
• Roasted Coconut & Spice Paste:
	• 3/4 to 1 cup fresh grated coconut
	• Whole spices (cinnamon, cloves, fennel seeds, coriander seeds, peppercorns)
	• Spice powders (turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala)
• Tempering (Tadka):
	• Coconut oil (2 to 3 tablespoons)
	• Mustard seeds (1 tsp)
	• Dried red chillies (1 to 2 nos)
	• Sliced shallots
	• Fresh curry leaves (2 sprigs)
• Salt & Water: As needed for pressure cooking and gravy
Recipes.instructions:
Making Puttu 
• Prepare the flour: Mix 1 cup of coarse rice flour with a pinch of salt and gradually sprinkle lukewarm water until the mixture resembles damp sand (it should hold its shape when pressed, yet crumble easily). Let it rest for 10 minutes.
• Layer the puttu maker: Place the perforated disc at the bottom of the puttu cylinder. Add a layer of grated coconut, followed by a layer of the moistened rice flour flour mixture, and alternate until the cylinder is full, ending with a final layer of coconut on top.
• Steam: Bring water to a boil in the puttu maker base, place the filled cylinder on top, and steam over medium-low heat for 5 to 7 minutes until steam escapes freely from the top.
• Unmold: Remove from heat, let it rest for 2 to 3 minutes, and gently push the cylindrical puttu out using a wooden spoon

Making Kadala Curry
• Soak and cook the chickpeas: Soak 1 cup of black chickpeas (kala chana) overnight or for 8 hours. Pressure cook the soaked chickpeas with 2 to 3 cups of water, 1 teaspoon of salt, and ½ teaspoon of turmeric powder for 5 to 6 whistles (or about 1 whistle on high then 4 on low) until completely soft.
• Prepare the roasted coconut masala: Heat 1 tablespoon of coconut oil in a pan. Roast grated coconut (about 4 tablespoons), shallots, dried red chilies, coriander seeds, fennel seeds, and curry leaves until deep golden-brown and aromatic. Let it cool, then blend into a smooth paste. Mash a small portion of the boiled chickpeas separately and add it to the paste to thicken the gravy.
• Sauté the aromatics: In a kadhai or pan, heat coconut oil and splutter mustard seeds. Add sliced onions (or shallots), ginger-garlic paste, slit green chilies, and curry leaves. Sauté until golden, then add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and mushy.
• Simmer the curry: Stir in turmeric powder, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Add the cooked black chickpeas along with their cooking liquid and the ground coconut-chickpea masala paste. Mix well, cover, and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes.
• Tempering: Heat a little coconut oil in a small pan, splutter mustard seeds, and fry sliced shallots, a dried red chili, and curry leaves. Pour this sizzling tempering over the curry, stir in 1 teaspoon of garam masala, and serve hot alongside your freshly steamed puttu
Recipes.description: Puttu and Kadala is a classic, traditional Kerala breakfast pairing consisting of Puttu (steamed rice cylinders layered with grated coconut) and Kadala Curry (a rich, spicy black chickpea gravy

Recipes.name: Pizza
Recipes.ingredients:
Pizza Dough
• Flour: All-purpose flour, bread flour, or Italian "00" flour
• Yeast: Active dry or instant yeast
• Water: Warm water to activate the yeast
• Oil: Olive oil or extra virgin olive oil
• Salt & Sugar: Salt for flavor and sugar to feed the yeast
• Dusting: Cornmeal or semolina flour for the pan

Pizza Sauce
• Tomatoes: Crushed tomatoes, San Marzano tomatoes, or canned tomato sauce
• Aromatics & Seasoning: Garlic, salt, black pepper, and sugar to balance acidity
• Herbs: Dried or fresh basil, oregano, and red pepper flakes
• Oil: Olive oil

Cheese
• Mozzarella: Low-moisture mozzarella, fresh mozzarella, or buffalo mozzarella
• Alternative / Extra Cheeses: Parmesan, cheddar, or fontina for extra melt and flavor

Toppings
• Meats: Pepperoni, Italian sausage, bacon, ham, or chicken
• Vegetables: Onions, bell peppers, mushrooms, olives, and fresh cherry tomatoes
• Other Favorites: Pineapple, sweet corn, or fresh basil leaves
Recipes.instructions:
Step-by-Step Instructions
• Prep the dough: Bring your homemade or store-bought dough to room temperature for 3 to 4 hours. Use your hands to gently stretch the dough into a 10- to 12-inch circle on a floured surface rather than using a rolling pin, which flattens out the air bubbles. For detailed guidelines, check out the Pizza Recipe Guide.
• Add toppings: Transfer the stretched dough to a cornmeal-dusted pizza peel. Spread a light layer of tomato sauce (about 1/3 to 1/2 cup), low-moisture mozzarella cheese, and your choice of toppings, keeping them light to prevent a soggy center.
• Bake the pizza: Slide the pizza off the peel onto the preheated baking stone or steel. Bake at 475°F to 550°F for 6 to 10 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbly. For larger batches or step-by-step techniques, see the Instructables Pizza Tutorial.
• Finish and serve: Drizzle the crust with extra virgin olive oil and a sprinkle of parmesan cheese, then rest it on a wire rack for 1 to 2 minutes before slicing
Recipes.description: Pizza is an oven-baked, flat, round bread dish topped with tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese, and various meats, vegetables, or herbs

Recipes.name: Shawarma
Recipes.ingredients:
Meat
• Chicken or Beef: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, or thin-cut beef/lamb.

Marinade
• Acid & Fat: Fresh lemon juice and extra virgin olive oil.
• Tenderizer: Plain yogurt (or buttermilk).
• Aromatics: Minced or crushed garlic.
• Warm Spices: Ground cumin, coriander, cardamom, paprika (or smoked paprika), cinnamon, and allspice.
• Heat & Seasoning: Salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper or chili flakes.

Bread & Assembly
• Flatbread: Pita bread, Lebanese flatbread, or lavash.
• Vegetables: Sliced tomatoes, red onions, shredded lettuce, cucumbers, and pickles.
• Sauce: Garlic sauce, tahini, or lemon-yogurt sauce
Recipes.instructions:
2. Marinate the Chicken
• Mix: In a large bowl or zip-top bag, combine the olive oil, lemon juice, yogurt, minced garlic, and all the spices.
• Coat: Add the chicken thighs and toss until every piece is completely covered.
• Rest: Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally overnight (up to 24 hours) for the best flavor.

3. Cooking Methods
Oven-Roasting Method
• Preheat: Heat your oven to 425°F (220°C).
• Arrange: Scatter the sliced onions in a greased baking sheet or cast-iron skillet, then place the marinated chicken thighs on top in a single layer.
• Roast: Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
• Broil: Switch the oven to broil for the last 5 to 8 minutes to get crisp, charred edges and caramelized onions.

Stovetop / Skillet Method
• Heat: Warm a heavy-duty cast-iron skillet or non-stick pan over medium-high heat with a little oil.
• Sear: Cook the chicken thighs for 4 to 5 minutes per side until dark char spots develop.
• Press (Optional): Press the thighs down with a weight or spatula to build an even crust.

Air-Fryer Method
• Preheat: Set your air fryer to 380°F to 400°F (190°C to 200°C).
• Cook: Place the chicken in the basket and air fry for 20 to 25 minutes (flipping halfway through), depending on the size of the pieces.

4. Rest and Slice
• Rest: Transfer the cooked chicken to a cutting board and tent loosely with foil for 5 to 7 minutes so the juices redistribute.
• Slice: Thinly slice the chicken across the grain and spoon any leftover pan juices over the meat
Recipes.description: Shawarma is a popular Middle Eastern street food consisting of thin slices of marinated meat stacked in an inverted cone and slow-roasted on a vertical rotisserie

Recipes.name: Poratta & Beef
Recipes.ingredients:
Porotta Ingredients
• Maida (Refined Wheat Flour): 500g (the base for the flaky layered flatbread)
• Water or Milk: About 230 ml (to knead the dough)
• Sugar: 1 teaspoon (for a touch of sweetness and browning)
• Salt: 1 teaspoon
• Egg: 1 (optional, helps soften the dough)
• Oil or Ghee: 4+ tablespoons (generously used for coating, resting, and frying the layers)

 Beef Roast / Fry Ingredients
• Beef: 500g to 1 kg (boneless chuck or braising beef, cut into small cubes)
• Aromatics & Base:
	• Sliced onions or shallots (1 to 2 large)
	• Ginger-garlic paste or freshly minced ginger and garlic (1 to 2 tablespoons)
	• Green chilies (2 to 3, slit)
	• Curry leaves (2 sprigs)
• Spice Powders:
	• Turmeric powder (½ teaspoon)
	• Chili powder or Kashmiri chili powder (1 teaspoon)
	• Coriander powder (1 to 2 tablespoons)
	• Black pepper powder or crushed black pepper (1 teaspoon)
	• Fennel powder or fennel seeds (½ to 1 teaspoon)
	• Garam masala or meat masala (1 teaspoon
Recipes.instructions:
Porotta Ingredients & Instructions
• Dough Ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour (maida), ½ tsp sugar, ½ tsp salt, 2–3 tbsp oil or ghee, and water as needed
• Kneading & Resting:
	• Combine flour, sugar, salt, and water, then knead well for 8–10 minutes until soft and elastic.
	• Divide the dough into equal portions (balls), generously coat them in oil or ghee, cover with a damp cloth, and let them rest for at least 1 hour.
• Layering & Cooking:
	• Flatten each dough ball, stretch it paper-thin on an oiled surface, pleat/fold it like a fan, and coil it into a circular spiral (snail shape).
	• Gently roll out the coiled dough into a flat disc.
	• Cook on a hot tawa or griddle with a little ghee or oil until golden brown spots appear on both sides.
	• While hot, gently crush or clap the porotta from the sides with your hands to open up the flaky layers.

Step-by-Step Instructions for Beef
1. Pressure Cook the Beef:
	• Clean the beef cubes and place them in a pressure cooker.
	• Add turmeric powder, chili powder, coriander powder, pepper powder, ginger-garlic paste, salt, and ¼ to ½ cup of water.
	• Cook for 4 to 6 whistles (or up to 10 whistles depending on the toughness of the meat) until tender. Reserve the beef stock.
2. Sauté the Aromatics:
	• Heat coconut oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or wok over medium heat.
	• Splutter fennel seeds, then add sliced shallots, ginger, garlic, green chilies, and curry leaves. Sauté until golden brown.
	• Optionally toss in thin coconut slices (thenga kothu) until lightly browned.
3. Add Spices and Roast:
	• Stir in coriander powder, Kashmiri chili powder, and meat masala. Cook for a minute until the raw smell fades.
	• Pour in the cooked beef along with its reserved stock.
	• Simmer on medium-low heat until the gravy thickens and clings to the meat, creating the signature rich, pepper-forward thattukada-style coating.
	• Finish with a sprinkle of freshly crushed black pepper, extra curry leaves, and a raw drop of coconut oil.
Recipes.description: Porotta and beef is the iconic culinary pairing of flaky, layered South Indian flatbread (Kerala porotta) served alongside spicy, dark-roasted beef curry or dry beef fry (Nadan beef ullarthiyatu)

Recipes.name: Chicken Curry
Recipes.ingredients:
• Chicken: 1 kg bone-in or boneless pieces (thighs and breasts work best)
• Aromatics & Base:
	• 2 to 4 finely chopped onions
	• 1 to 2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste (or fresh minced ginger and garlic)
	• 2 to 3 chopped tomatoes or tomato puree
	• 1 to 2 green chilies
• Whole Spices (for tempering):
	• 1 bay leaf
	• 1 inch cinnamon stick
	• 3 to 4 cloves
	• 2 to 3 green cardamoms
	• 1 teaspoon cumin seeds
• Ground Spices:
	• 1 to 2 teaspoons turmeric powder
	• 1 to 2 teaspoons red chili powder (or Kashmiri chili powder for color)
	• 1.5 to 2 teaspoons coriander powder
	• 1/2 to 1 teaspoon garam masala
• Liquid & Fat:
	• 3 to 4 tablespoons cooking oil or ghee
	• 1/2 cup plain yogurt, curd, or coconut milk (optional, for a creamy base)
	• 1 to 2 cups water or chicken stock
• Garnish:
	• Freshly chopped coriander leaves
	• Lemon juice
Recipes.instructions:
1. Sauté Whole Spices: Heat oil or ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds, bay leaf, cinnamon stick, cloves, and cardamom. Let them sizzle for a few seconds.
2. Cook the Onions: Add the finely chopped onions and a pinch of salt. Sauté until they turn golden brown (about 5 to 7 minutes).
3. Add Aromatics: Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the raw smell disappears.
4. Build the Masala Base: Add the chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Cook until the tomatoes turn mushy and oil begins to separate from the masala.
5. Sear the Chicken: Add the chicken pieces to the pan. Fry on medium-high heat for 5 minutes so the chicken absorbs the spices and changes color.
6. Simmer the Curry: Pour in 1 cup of warm water and stir well. Cover the pan with a lid, reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
7. Finish and Garnish: Sprinkle garam masala over the top and stir well. Turn off the heat and garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Recipes.description: Chicken curry is a popular dish featuring tender pieces of chicken stewed in a savory, spiced gravy made from a base of onions, tomatoes, ginger, and garlic

Recipes.name: Pazham Pori
Recipes.ingredients:
• Banana: Ripe Nendram plantains / bananas (yellow with black spots)
• All-Purpose Flour (Maida): 1 cup (or 0.5 to 1.5 cups depending on batch size)
• Rice Flour: 2 to 3 tablespoons (used for crispiness)
• Sugar or Jaggery Powder: 2 to 3 tablespoons
• Turmeric Powder: A pinch (for a natural yellow color)
• Cardamom Powder: ¼ teaspoon (optional, for aroma)
• Salt: A pinch
• Baking Soda / Baking Powder: A pinch
• Water: As needed to make a smooth, thick batter (dosa or pancake batter consistency)
• Oil: Coconut oil (recommended for traditional flavor) or high-smoke vegetable oil for deep frying
Recipes.instructions:
1. Prepare the Batter:
• In a mixing bowl, combine the maida, rice flour, sugar (or jaggery powder), turmeric powder, cardamom powder, and a pinch of salt.
• Gradually add water and whisk well until you get a smooth, thick coating consistency similar to dosa or cake batter (not too watery). 
2. Slice the Bananas:
	• Peel the ripe Nendran bananas.
	• Cut each banana in half crosswise, then slice each half lengthwise into thick pieces (about 2 to 4 vertical slices per half).
3. Heat the Oil:
	• Heat enough oil for deep frying in a wide pan or kadai over medium heat.
4. Coat and Fry:
	• Dip each banana slice into the prepared batter, making sure it is thoroughly and evenly coated.
	• Gently slide the coated slices into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan; fry a few pieces at a time.
	• Fry on medium heat until the bottom turns golden brown, then flip gently to cook the other side.
5. Drain and Serve:
	• Remove the golden-brown fritters with a slotted spoon and drain them on paper towels to remove excess oil.
	• Serve hot or warm alongside a cup of evening tea or coffee
Recipes.description: Pazham Pori is a traditional South Indian deep-fried banana fritter snack from Kerala

Recipes.name: onion vada
Recipes.ingredients:
• Onions: 3 to 5 medium-sized onions, thinly sliced
• Flours:
	• Gram flour (besan) for binding and texture
	• All-purpose flour (maida)
	• Rice flour for crispiness
• Aromatics & Herbs:
	• Finely chopped green chilies (2 to 4 nos)
	• Chopped or grated ginger (1 inch piece)
	• Fresh curry leaves (a few sprigs)
	• Fresh coriander leaves (optional)
• Spices & Seasoning:
	• Red chili powder (1/4 to 1 tsp)
	• Turmeric powder (a pinch, optional)
	• Asafoetida (hing, 2 pinches)
	• Fennel seeds (perunjeerakam, optional for aroma)
	• Salt to taste
Recipes.instructions:
1. Squeeze the Onions:
	• Place the thinly sliced onions in a mixing bowl with the salt.
	• Massage and squeeze the onions well with your hands for a couple of minutes so they soften and release their natural moisture.
2. Add Spices and Herbs:
	• Add the finely chopped green chilies, ginger, curry leaves, coriander leaves, fennel seeds, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and asafoetida. Mix everything thoroughly.
3. Incorporate the Flours:
	• Sprinkle in the maida, rice flour, and besan.
	• Bind the mixture together using the moisture from the onions. Do not add extra water unless the mixture is too dry to hold its shape. It should form a dense, stiff clump.
4. Shape the Vadas:
	• Heat oil in a kadai or deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
	• Grease your hands with a little oil. Take small, lemon-sized portions of the mixture and gently flatten or shape them into rough patties.
5. Deep Fry:
	• Gently drop the shaped vadas into the hot oil.
	• Fry on medium-low heat, turning occasionally, until they turn crisp and golden brown.
	• Remove them with a slotted spoon and drain excess oil on paper towels
Recipes.description: Ullivada (also spelled Ulli Vada) is a popular traditional South Indian and Kerala-style evening snack made from thinly sliced onions mixed with flours and spices, then deep-fried until crisp.

Recipes.name: Veg-Samoosa
Recipes.ingredients:
For the Dough (Crust)
• All-purpose flour (Maida): 2 cups
• Carom seeds (Ajwain): 3/4 to 1 tsp
• Ghee or oil: 1/4 cup (melted, for a flaky texture)
• Salt: 3/4 tsp
• Water: 4 to 6 tbsp (used gradually to make a stiff dough)

For the Potato Filling (Masala)
• Potatoes: 500g (about 3-4 medium, boiled, peeled, and coarsely mashed)
• Green peas: 1/2 cup (fresh or frozen)
• Cumin seeds: 3/4 to 1 tsp
• Fennel seeds: 1/2 tsp
• Ginger: 1 tbsp (grated or finely chopped)
• Green chilies: 1-2 (finely chopped)
• Garam masala: 3/4 to 1 tsp
• Coriander powder: 1 tsp
• Cumin powder: 1/2 tsp
• Red chili powder: 3/4 to 1/2 tsp
• Amchur (dried mango powder) or lemon juice: 1/2 to 1 tsp (for tanginess)
• Salt: To taste
• Fresh coriander leaves (Cilantro): Finely chopped
• Oil: 1 to 2 tablespoons (for sautéing the filling)
Recipes.instructions:
1. Make the Samosa Dough
• Ingredients:
	• 2 cups (approx. 260g) all-purpose flour (maida)
	• 1 tsp carom seeds (ajwain) or cumin seeds
	• ½ tsp salt
	• 4 tbsp oil or melted ghee (for shortening)
	• ~6 tbsp water (add gradually)
• Instructions:
	1. Mix the flour, salt, and ajwain in a large bowl. Rub the oil or ghee into the flour with your fingertips until it resembles breadcrumbs and holds its shape when squeezed.
	2. Slowly add water and knead into a firm, stiff dough (do not make it soft like bread dough).
	3. Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for 30 to 40 minutes.

2. Prepare the Potato Filling
• Ingredients:
	• 3 to 4 large boiled and roughly mashed potatoes (about 500g)
	• ½ cup green peas (fresh or thawed)
	• 2 tbsp oil
	• 1 tsp cumin seeds or fennel seeds
	• 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste and finely chopped green chilies
• Spices:
	• 1–2 tsp crushed coriander seeds
	• 1 tsp coriander powder
	• ½ tsp garam masala
	• ½ tsp dry mango powder (amchur) or a squeeze of lemon juice
	• ½ tsp red chili powder and salt to taste
• Instructions:
	1. Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Add cumin/fennel seeds and let them crackle.
	2. Add the ginger, garlic, and green chilies; sauté for a few seconds.
	3. Add the green peas, mashed potatoes, and all the dry spices.
	4. Stir well and cook for 2–3 minutes so the flavors blend. Remove from heat and let the filling cool completely.

3. Shape and Fill the Samosas
1. Divide the rested dough into 6 to 7 equal balls (about 58–60g each).
2. Roll out one ball into a thin oval shape (about 6 inches long and 1/16-inch thick).
3. Cut the oval cleanly in half with a knife.
4. Take one half-circle, brush a little water along the straight edge, and fold it into a cone shape, pressing the seam firmly to seal.
5. Stuff the cone with 1.5 to 2 tablespoons of the potato filling (do not overstuff).
6. Apply a little water around the inner top edges, make a small pleat at the back edge, and press the front and back edges tightly together to seal the pocket. Repeat with the remaining dough.

4. Fry or Bake
• Deep Frying (Traditional):
	1. Heat oil in a deep kadhai or pan on low to medium-low heat. The oil should be gently warm (around 285°F–300°F to start) so the crust doesn't bubble or turn soggy on the outside.
	2. Drop 4–5 samosas in at a time and fry slowly on low heat for 10–12 minutes, turning occasionally, until light golden. Raise the heat slightly toward the end until they turn deep golden brown and crisp.
	3. Drain on paper towels
Recipes.description: A samosa is a fried or baked savory pastry with a distinct triangular, cone, or half-moon shape. It features a crisp, flaky shell made from refined wheat flour (maida) and an interior packed with a seasoned filling

Recipes.name: Masala-Bonda
Recipes.ingredients:
Potato Masala Filling
• Potatoes: 3 to 4 medium, boiled and mashed
• Oil: 1 to 2 tablespoons (traditionally coconut oil in Kerala homes)
• Mustard Seeds: 1/2 teaspoon
• Fennel Seeds: 1 teaspoon (optional/regional variation)
• Curry Leaves: 1 sprig, fresh
• Onion: 1 medium, finely chopped
• Ginger: 1 teaspoon, grated or finely chopped
• Green Chillies: 2, finely chopped
• Turmeric Powder: 1/4 teaspoon
• Garam Masala / Chili Powder: 1/2 teaspoon (optional, depending on spice preference)
• Coriander Leaves: 2 tablespoons, chopped
• Salt: To taste

Outer Batter Coating
• Besan (Gram Flour): 3/4 cup
• Rice Flour: 2 tablespoons (adds extra crispness)
• Red Chilli Powder: 1/2 teaspoon
• Turmeric Powder: A pinch
• Baking Soda: A pinch (for a light, fluffy lift)
• Salt: To taste
• Water: About 1/2 cup (to form a thick, smooth coating consistency
Recipes.instructions:
Make the Potato Filling
	• Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a pan over medium heat.
	• Add the mustard seeds; once they start to pop, throw in the curry leaves.
	• Add the chopped onion, ginger, and green chillies. Sauté for 3 to 4 minutes until the onions soften.
	• Stir in the turmeric powder and salt, then add the mashed potatoes.
	• Mix thoroughly, cook for 2 minutes, stir in the fresh coriander leaves, and turn off the heat. Let the mixture cool completely.
Shape the Bonda Balls
	• Divide the cooled potato mixture into 12 to 14 equal portions.
	• Roll each portion into a smooth, round ball using lightly greased palms. Chill them in the refrigerator for about 10 minutes to help them hold their shape.
 Prepare the Batter
	• In a mixing bowl, combine the besan, rice flour, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, baking soda, and salt.
	• Gradually add water a little at a time, whisking continuously to make a thick, smooth batter (it should comfortably coat the back of a spoon without being too watery).
 Heat the Oil
	• Pour 450 ml of oil into a deep kadai or pan over medium heat.
	• Test the oil by dropping a tiny speck of batter into it; if it rises steadily to the surface, the oil is ready. Keep the flame at medium.
 Dip and Fry
	• Take each potato ball and dip it into the besan batter, turning it around until it is completely and evenly coated.
	• Gently slide 5 or 6 coated balls into the hot oil from the edge of the pan to avoid splattering.
	• Fry for 5 to 6 minutes, turning them gently every minute or so, until they turn a deep golden brown and crisp.
	• Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper
Recipes.description: A Kerala-style masala bonda (often found at local thattukada roadside tea shops) is a popular deep-fried South Indian snack featuring a spiced potato center wrapped in a crisp, savory batter
